# Specification title

## Purpose and scope

State the problem, affected consumers and explicit boundaries. Link the current project standards and governing ADRs.

## Requirements and assumptions

Give each requirement an ID. Separate confirmed requirements from proposed defaults and assumptions requiring evidence.

## Contract and behavior

Describe inputs, outputs, errors, state transitions, authorization and compatibility/version effects. Link the canonical schema rather than duplicate it. Include Mermaid diagrams where useful.

## Security, privacy and lifecycle

Describe tenant/residency boundaries, classified fields, telemetry, erasure, identity and trust changes.

## Operations and delivery

Describe environment impact, quotas, capacity, migrations, rollout, rollback and supported-version obligations.

## Acceptance evidence

List observable success/failure criteria and real boundary tests. Separate planned validation from executed results.

## Alternatives and open decisions

Explain trade-offs; link durable decisions and owned follow-ups.
